problem: Zero-shot VLN work mostly targets discrete nav-graph environments that assume collision-free moves between nodes, so it ignores collisions in continuous environments (VLN-CE), where low-level movement can hit obstacles.
motivation: Instruction-path annotation is expensive, and general-purpose agents should navigate unfamiliar environments without task-specific training. Continuous navigation needs both a direction and a safe travel distance.
key_idea: Use foundation models zero-shot to pick a direction (LLM-extracted attention spots matched to panorama views with CLIP), and a learned depth-based occupancy predictor to choose a collision-free distance.
insight: The ablation shows collision mitigation matters most: removing OMP drops SR from 0.11 to 0.01 and raises collisions from 0.67 to 3.07. Removing ASP as well drives SR to 0 and collisions to 24.49. Absolute performance is still low (SPL 0.02), so direction selection remains the weak point.
method: Attention Spot Predictor (ASP): an LLM (ChatGPT 3.5) splits the instruction into attention spots (objects or scenes at the next location, e.g. a yellow door).
View Selector (VS): CLIP similarity between the current attention spot and the 12 panorama views at 30° intervals; the best view's angle becomes the heading.
Progress Monitor (PM): rule-based; if the similarity between the current spot and the views decreases consecutively, the spot is treated as passed and the next spot becomes the target.

Open Map Predictor (OMP): a transformer (following the DUET/hong2022bridging-style architecture) takes 12 depth panorama images and predicts an occupancy mask over 120 angles and 12 distances, trained on Habitat-based data.
Distance selection: choose the collision-free distance along the selected direction from the occupancy mask.

setting.backbone: ChatGPT 3.5 (frozen) + CLIP (frozen) + transformer OMP (trained on Habitat data)
setting.training_data: Only the OMP is trained, on a Habitat-simulator-derived dataset of depth panoramas with collision-free distance labels; the LLM and CLIP are used zero-shot (no instruction-path data).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (12 views at 30°) + panoramic depth
setting.action_space: predicted direction (30° increments) and distance, executed as low-level actions in VLN-CE

numbers.extra: OMP trained on Habitat-derived depth data; SR/SPL printed as fractions; collision rate 0.67 from ablation table
numbers.evidence: Table 1 comparison with baselines and Table 2 ablation: VLN-CM 0.11 / 0.02 / 0.67

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0.11), not percentages. The paper says only 'validation data' / 'unseen dataset', so val-unseen is assumed. Whether the full split was used is not stated.
results: VLN-CM reaches SR 0.11 versus 0.03 for both the Random and Hand-Crafted agents, though its SPL is 0.02, the same as theirs. Removing OMP raises collisions from 0.67 to 3.07 and cuts SR to 0.01.
limitations: Very low absolute performance (SR 0.11, SPL 0.02) and only trivial baselines, with no comparison to trained or other zero-shot VLN-CE methods
The paper is short, with sparse details (OMP training data size, metric definitions, and the collision-rate unit are not given)
The rule-based progress monitor and CLIP matching are brittle for complex instructions
